hero.title: Festivals in Mauritius 2026
hero.subtitle: Experience the vibrant multicultural celebrations of our island paradise with current-year dates.

intro.title: A Melting Pot of Cultures
intro.p1Before: Mauritius prides itself on being a
intro.p1After: , where people of different religions, languages and cultures co-exist in one community.
intro.p2: The island's history brought together French, British, African, Indian and Chinese influences, each leaving traditions that still shape daily life.
intro.p3After: with celebrations that are colourful, spiritual and deeply rooted in local family life.

grid.title: Annual Celebrations
grid.subtitle: 2026 public holiday dates are listed where available. Eid dates may still depend on official moon-sighting confirmation.

cta.title: Experience Mauritius Culture
cta.body: Plan your visit during one of our vibrant festivals and immerse yourself in the rich cultural heritage of Mauritius.

items.name: New Year's Eve
items.description: Mauritius celebrates New Year's Eve with beach dinners, resort events and fireworks along the coast.
items.visitorTip: Reserve beach dinners early and ask your hotel which fireworks spots are easiest to reach.
items.imageAlt: New Year's Eve celebrations in Mauritius

items.name: Spring Festival (Chinese New Year)
items.description: Chinese New Year brings lion dances, dragon dances, red lanterns and festive food around Port Louis and Chinatown.
items.visitorTip: Go to Port Louis or Chinatown in the morning for colour, food stalls and lion-dance atmosphere.
items.imageAlt: Chinese New Year celebrations in Mauritius

items.name: Abolition of Slavery
items.description: This public holiday remembers the abolition of slavery and an important turning point in Mauritius history.
items.visitorTip: Pair the date with Le Morne Brabant to understand the island's maroon history and UNESCO story.
items.imageAlt: Abolition of Slavery remembrance in Mauritius

items.name: Thaipusam Cavadee
items.description: A major Tamil festival marked by fasting, offerings, processions and powerful devotion around temples.
items.visitorTip: Watch respectfully near Tamil temples, dress modestly and avoid blocking processions.

items.name: Maha Shivaratree
items.description: Devotees walk to Grand Bassin carrying decorated kanwars to honour Lord Shiva at the sacred lake.
items.visitorTip: Grand Bassin is powerful but busy; expect traffic and visit with quiet, respectful behaviour.
items.imageAlt: Maha Shivaratree pilgrimage to Grand Bassin

items.name: Holi
items.description: Holi celebrates the victory of good over evil with bonfires, colour powder and joyful community gatherings.
items.visitorTip: Join only when invited, protect cameras and wear clothes you do not mind staining.

items.name: Independence Day
items.description: Mauritians mark independence with flags, public ceremonies and local gatherings across the island.
items.visitorTip: Look for flags, local gatherings and official ceremonies, especially around towns and schools.

items.name: Ugaadi
items.description: Ugaadi marks New Year for Deccan communities and is observed through family and temple traditions.
items.visitorTip: This is more family and temple focused than a tourist spectacle, so observe quietly if invited.

items.name: Eid-ul-Fitr
items.description: Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan with prayers, family gatherings and festive meals.
items.visitorTip: Dates can shift with moon sighting; expect family gatherings, mosque activity and festive meals.

items.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
items.description: Ganesh Chaturthi honours Ganesha with prayers, temporary shrines and community processions.
items.visitorTip: Look for temple and community processions, and ask before photographing worshippers.

items.name: Pere Laval Pilgrimage
items.description: People of many faiths visit the shrine of Pere Laval in Sainte Croix, Port Louis.
items.visitorTip: Sainte Croix is busiest around the vigil and feast day; go slowly and follow crowd guidance.

items.name: Diwali
items.description: Diwali lights homes and neighbourhoods with lamps, sweets and the celebration of light over darkness.
items.visitorTip: Walk neighbourhoods respectfully after dark, enjoy the lights and accept sweets only when offered.

faqs.question: Do I need a visa for Mauritius?
faqs.answer: It depends on your nationality. Many visitor nationalities can enter Mauritius without a visa, some receive a visa on arrival, and a smaller group must apply before travel. Use the country list on this page and confirm with the official Passport and Immigration Office before booking.

faqs.question: Is the Mauritius visa free?
faqs.answer: Mauritius visas and extensions of stay are issued free of charge according to the official Passport and Immigration Office guidance.

faqs.question: How long can I stay in Mauritius as a tourist?
faqs.answer: A tourist stay can be granted for up to six months per calendar year on a case-by-case basis. Final admission and length of stay are always decided by the Immigration Officer.

important.title: Important Information
items: A visa allows you to travel to Mauritius but does not guarantee entry. Final admission is at the discretion of the Immigration Officer.
Visas and extensions of stay are issued free of charge.
Travellers without a required visa may be repatriated at the carrier's cost.
Overstaying your visa period is an offence and may result in prosecution.
Students should only travel after their study application has been approved.
Holders of EU passports and diplomatic passports, except certain countries, are exempt from visa regulations.

metadata.title: Best Time to Visit Mauritius
metadata.description: The best time to visit Mauritius by season, month, weather, cyclone risk, activities and travel budget.

hero.title: Best Time to Visit Mauritius
hero.subtitle: Year-round sunshine awaits. Discover when to visit for your perfect holiday experience.

intro.title: When is the best time to visit Mauritius?
intro.p1Before: This is one of the questions travellers ask most often. The short answer:
intro.bestMonths: April, May, September, October and November
intro.p1After: usually give the best balance of sunshine, comfortable temperatures and better-value flights or hotels.
intro.p2: Whatever time of the year you visit, Mauritius weather is sure to put on a show. Mauritius offers year-round holiday weather, with almost daily sunshine and limited rainfall, so you are almost guaranteed sunny days on your holiday.
intro.mythTitle: The myth: When is the rainy season in Mauritius?
intro.p3: Mauritius is a subtropical island, so it does not have a classic monsoon season. In summer, humidity can build into short, heavy afternoon showers, and cyclones can affect the weather between December and March. It is worth planning with flexibility, especially for boat trips, hikes and long coastal drives.

BestTimeToVisit.monthSummarySubtitle: A quick month-by-month view of weather, crowds and what is happening on the island.

monthSummaries.summary: Hot, humid and lively, with warm lagoons and New Year crowds. Afternoon showers are common, and cyclone alerts are worth watching before boat trips or long drives.
Still peak summer: warm seas, tropical rain bursts and busy school-holiday energy. Maha Shivaratree and Cavadee can bring memorable cultural moments and extra road traffic.
A warm shoulder month with softer crowds after the holiday rush. Expect swimming-friendly sea temperatures, occasional heavy showers and Independence Day celebrations around March 12.
One of the best all-round months: warm water, calmer humidity and fewer cyclone concerns. Crowds ease after Easter periods, making it strong for families and honeymoons.
Dry, bright and comfortable, with excellent beach weather and better-value stays. It is a sweet spot for road trips, hiking and west-coast sunsets before winter winds build.
Cooler, drier and usually good value, especially away from school breaks. Lagoons stay pleasant, hiking is comfortable and whale season begins on the west coast.
A breezy winter month with cooler evenings and reliable dry spells. East and south-east coasts can be windier, while Le Morne becomes popular for kite and wind sports.
Dry and windy in places, with European summer-holiday demand lifting crowds and rates. Choose sheltered north or west beaches if swimming is your priority.
A favourite shoulder month: low humidity, brighter days and improving warmth. It is excellent for hikes, coastal drives and Pere Laval pilgrimage dates near Port Louis.
Sunny, warm and often calm before the full summer heat returns. Clear water, lighter crowds and rising temperatures make it one of the easiest months to recommend.
Summer begins with warmer seas, greener landscapes and more humidity. Diwali often lights up neighbourhoods, while early booking helps before festive-season prices rise.
Festive, hot and high demand, especially around Christmas and New Year. Book hotels and restaurants early, and keep an eye on weather updates for tropical systems.

BestTimeToVisit.faqTitle: Best Time to Visit Mauritius FAQ

faqs.question: What is cyclone season in Mauritius?
faqs.answer: Cyclone season in Mauritius usually runs from November to April, with the highest risk from January to March. Serious cyclones are not constant, but travellers should follow official weather alerts before boat trips, hikes and coastal drives.

faqs.question: When is the rainy season in Mauritius?
faqs.answer: Mauritius does not have a monsoon season. The warmer summer months from November to April bring more humidity and short heavy showers, especially in the afternoon, while May to October is usually cooler and drier.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest month to visit Mauritius?
faqs.answer: The best value is often found in shoulder months such as May, June, September and early October, outside major school holidays and peak festive travel periods.

faqs.question: What is the best month to visit Mauritius?
faqs.answer: May, June, September and October usually give the best balance of pleasant weather, lower humidity and good prices. November to April is warmer for swimming but can be wetter.

seasonCopy.title: What's the seasons like?
seasonCopy.p1: For starters, summer is between November and March, and winter is between June and August.
seasonCopy.summerBody: is the warmest time of the year, with average overnight temperatures around 25 degrees and daytime averages around 30 degrees. It is a busy period for locals and visitors, with swimming, barbecues and water activities popular across the island. Humidity can be high, brief afternoon rain is normal, and this is also the main cyclone period, so use the live weather chart before travelling long distances or booking sea trips.
seasonCopy.autumnBody: is the transition from hot summer days to calmer blue skies with little wind. April and May are often excellent for families, honeymoons, fishing, beach days and clear water, with far fewer cyclone concerns.
seasonCopy.winterBefore: It has to be said that
seasonCopy.winterBody: in Mauritius is very mild, with coastal temperatures often around 22°C to 25°C and rarely below 18°C. It is a great season for hiking, camping, waterfalls, whale watching, kitesurfing and windsurfing, especially around Le Morne and the south-west lagoons.
seasonCopy.p5: During winter, Mauritius becomes a paradise for sailing and wind-sport enthusiasts.
seasonCopy.springBody: with improving weather through September and October. Days become warmer, humidity remains low, and the island is usually dry and bright.

mythBox.title: Common Myth: "Rainy Season"
mythBox.bold: There is no rainy season in Mauritius.
mythBox.body: Being a subtropical island, Mauritius does not have monsoon seasons. In summer, brief afternoon rain can occur because of humidity, but these showers often last just an hour or two. Mauritius offers year-round holiday weather with almost daily sunshine.

months.description: January is peak summer in Mauritius: hot, humid and lively. Expect warm lagoons, short tropical showers and New Year crowds. Chinese New Year can bring dragon dances, fireworks and red lanterns to towns across the island.

months.name: February
months.description: February remains hot and tropical, with warm ocean water and short rain bursts. It suits romantic trips, diving, snorkelling and resort stays, but keep plans flexible during cyclone season.

months.name: March
months.description: March is a warm shoulder month as summer softens. The island is green, waterfalls are flowing and crowds ease after the holiday rush, making it good for beaches, hikes and road trips.

months.name: April
months.description: April is one of the best all-round months. Weather is warm but calmer, humidity drops and cyclone risk is very low. It is excellent for families, honeymoons, beaches and nature days.

months.name: May
months.description: May is dry, bright and comfortable. It is a sweet spot for road trips, hiking, Chamarel, waterfall chasing and west-coast sunsets, often with better value and fewer visitors.

months.name: June
months.description: June starts the mild Mauritian winter. Days are cooler and drier, sightseeing is comfortable and whale season begins on the west coast.

months.name: July
months.description: July is cool, dry and breezy. It is ideal for active travellers, hikes and wind sports, while sheltered north and west beaches are better for swimming.

months.name: August
months.description: August is a popular winter month with sunny days, low humidity and more wind on the east coast. The west and north are warmer and calmer for beach days.

months.name: September
months.description: September is a favourite shoulder month with low humidity, bright days and warming seas. It is excellent for snorkelling, diving, dolphin watching, cruises and coastal drives.

months.name: October
months.description: October is sunny, warm and often calm before full summer heat returns. Clear water, lighter crowds and reliable sunshine make it one of the easiest months to recommend.

months.name: November
months.description: November brings warmer seas, greener landscapes and early summer energy before December peak prices. It is great for beaches, dolphin watching, water sports and island excursions.

months.name: December
months.description: December is festive, hot and high demand. Book hotels, restaurants and activities early, and watch tropical weather updates around Christmas and New Year.

Footer.tagline: Your guide to discovering the beauty of Mauritius. From pristine beaches to lush mountains, explore everything this island paradise has to offer.
